newsitem.title: USA: Flinn must repay Air Force for part of education.
newsitem.headline: Flinn must repay Air Force for part of education.

text.p: Air Force Lt. Kelly Flynn avoided a court martial, but will have to repay the service up to $19,000 for part of her education and will get no veteran's benefits under the terms of her resignation, Air Force officials said on Thursday.

Because Flinn accepted a general discharge and "resigned in lieu of a court martial" -- a step known as "RILO" in the Air Force -- she will also lose all medical and other special benefits that veterans receive, said the officials, who asked not to be identified.

They told reporters that because Flinn, 26, had fulfilled only four of the five years that she promised to serve on her 1993 graduation from the Air Force Academy, she would have to repay about 20 percent of the high cost of that education.
That repayment could total "between $18,000 and $19,000" said one of the officials.
The officials said Flinn could leave the Air Force within two or three weeks and would get full pay and benefits until that time, along with the cost of moving her personal effects.

Flinn, who faced charges of adultery, fraternisation, disobeying an order and lying to investigators, agreed on Thursday to leave the service with "a general discharge under honourable circumstances."
That general discharge, unlike a more favourable "honorable discharge", carries with it a stigma suggesting "negative aspects" of performance of duty, officials said.

Officials said that the general discharge would prevent her from joining the Air Force Reserve or National Guard without a special waiver. Flinn, the service's first woman B-52 bomber pilot, expressed interest in joining the reserves.

She will be provided with a "DD Form 214" upon her discharge that will show that the left the Air Force with a general discharge under honourable circumstances. It will include a special code which notes that she left to avoid a court martial.
"Under honourable conditions, a general discharge is separation from the Air Force with honour, but to a lesser degree than an honourable discharge," said one official.
"This (general) discharge is given when normally faithful service is marred by negative aspects of a person's duty, performance or personal conduct."
